overview: In a reversal of his usual style, Sagat is a projectile zoner second and a brawler first with an emphasis on scary, safe pressure moves that make him a true titan up close. With excellent offensive and defensive tools, Sagat controls the screen with his superior battle prowess while giving up nothing when up close.

What you'll likely notice first about Sagat is his enormous frame. Easily the largest character on the roster, Sagat stands tall above his foes. This frame gives Sagat excellent poking normals, such as his 5HP, 5MK, and 2MK, all of which have ludicrous reach. Once Sagat has claimed the space in front of him as his own, he can begin layering in his strong zoning game. Sagat's signature move is his infamous Tiger Shot, fast projectiles that can be fired from either chest or knee height. Each version of Tiger Shot has its own purpose; the LP version forces opponents to block and prevents low-profile evasion, the MP version travels slower for lockdown zoning and midscreen juggle extensions, and the HP version is ludicrously fast and stuffs any opponent that tries to jump on reaction. Of course, tigers love to pounce on their prey, and Sagat is no different. Once the opponent is conditioned to sit still and duck under MP/HP Tiger Shot, Sagat can leap forward with Tiger Knee, an advancing knee strike that's plus against crouch block.

If allowed to close the distance, Sagat has a number of excellent pressure options to rip his opponent to shreds. His 5MP is +2, MP Tiger Shot is plus if stand blocked, 6HK leaves him at +4 on stand block, and Tiger Knee can be spaced for frame advantage as well. Most terrifying of all is Sagat's new special Tiger Nexus, a Rekka-like move similar to Ken's Jinrai Kick. Upon hitting the opponent, Sagat can follow up with three options. The 6LK ender is an overhead that frame traps on block and knocks down on Counter-hit, the 6MK ender knocks down and give amazing block advantage but whiffs on crouchers, and the 6HK ender gives a full juggle launch anywhere on-screen while remaining plus on block, but has slow interruptible startup. Mixing between the various follow-ups forces opponents to decide whether they want to mitigate any potential damage, or prevent Sagat from scoring endless plus frames to drain their Drive gauge.

Speaking of juggles, Sagat has some of the best corner carry in the game, with 6HK, Tiger Knee, and Tiger Uppercut all functioning as extremely far traveling combo extenders/enders, allowing Sagat to quickly corner and pressure opponents. Another one of his most important combo moves is Tiger Monolith (4HP), a reliable anti air normal that also grants extremely high damage combos and gives him some big launches from Nova. This move also lets Sagat reliably combo into charged hp uppercut, which can quickly obliterate enemy health at the cost of worse okizeme.

Sagat boasts high damage whenever he lands a clean hit. He can spend Drive meter in a plethora of ways, including OD High Tiger Shot which juggles into Level 1 Super anywhere on screen. He has two meterless launchers in 4HP and Nova Tiger, both of which grant amazing corner carry with as little as 1 additional Drive bar. Sagat's Level 2 Super has four different follow-ups based on the direction held, giving him the option to pursue damage/corner carry, oki, a side swap, or a juggle launcher that lets Sagat dump additional resources to get the best of all worlds. All of this leads to an offense truly fit for a king, with exceptional reward once Sagat finds a hit.

However, as implied before, Sagat is sorely lacking in threatening lows for offense. While his 2LK can begin a light chain as is the standard, his movement speed and relatively poor midscreen oki makes it difficult to convert properly, it also makes neutral difficult if solely relying on buttons since most opponents will be faster than him which can lead to whiff punishers having a field day with Sagat if poorly conditioned. 2MK is not special cancelable, and does a poor job of maintaining Drive Rush momentum to initiate pressure, and while 6LK is a good standing low, it is fairly reactable and only grants links with Counter-hit, Drive Rush, or meaty timing. Crouching opponents can avoid many of Sagat's strongest tools, including MP/HP Tiger Shot, 6HK, and Greedy Tiger. Sagat must encourage opponents to stand by poking with lows to the best of his ability, and by threatening from a distance with Tiger Knee. Sagat is generally very committal, with slow movement, expensive throw loops, slow reversals, and slow Super Arts, with plenty of ways to punish him if he isn't cautious. Sagat's strong offense requires equally strong foresight from the player. If you like big normals, calculated zoning, excellent pressure, and Muay Thai in general, Sagat will show you how to become a true king.

pick.title: Everything The Light Touches
pick.text: Tricky projectile patterns, rewarding anti-airs, and massive pokes with confirmable knockdowns come together to give Sagat incredible space control, leaving no place on the screen truly safe.

pick.title: Crippling Power
pick.text: An array of pressure tools that can open up overly defensive opponents.

pick.title: Court Juggler
pick.text: Meterless launchers with plenty of options afterward, letting Sagat cash out his resources for huge damage and corner carry if he desires.

avoid.title: Moves One Space at a Time
avoid.text: Slower than average movement, often relying on Tiger Knee Crush or Drive Rush to move around

avoid.title: Uprisings and Downfalls
avoid.text: Conditioning your opponents to stand and crouch on demand to make your tools work to their fullest potential

avoid.title: No Bowing
avoid.text: Mediocre low options in pressure, and a throw that does not lead to a meterless throw loop

moves.name: Savage Tiger
moves.notes: Goes into one of 4 follow-ups after frame 76 on hit (depending on which direction is held while clutching the opponent); Sagat's best reversal Super (but is still slow enough to be baited by an opponent's safejab setup); can be used as a projectile counter from about half screen; Sagat has travel time throughout the active frames (takes longer than SA3 to reach full range)

moves.name: Savage Tiger Stomp (Oki)
moves.notes: Leaves the opponent close to Sagat for stronger oki than other versions; can walk up for a strike/throw/shimmy mixup; gives enough advantage for an immediate 6MP overhead

moves.name: Savage Tiger Pendulum (Side Switch)
moves.notes: Switches sides with opponent; leaves the opponent far away with no oki

moves.name: Savage Tiger Raid (Damage)
moves.notes: Highest damage variant of SA2; leaves the opponent far away with no oki; has significant corner carry (over 1/2 screen)

moves.name: Savage Tiger Zenith (Launcher)
moves.notes: Launches the opponent into a limited juggle state (juggle counter is always set to 2 regardless of previous juggle state); Hard Knockdown if the opponent hits the ground instead of being juggled; useful for corner carry, building back some Super gauge, and getting a good mix of damage + oki (but usually results in less damage than Tiger Raid)

moves.name: Tiger Nexus
moves.notes: Slow startup, only combos naturally from the first hit of 5HK (requires Drive Rush or Punish Counter to combo from 2HP, 4HP launch, or 5HK 2nd hit); 214HK cannot frame trap when canceled from a normal (except for Burnout + Drive Rush into 2MP/2HP/5HK); combos naturally into all follow-ups including 6HK; cancel into 6HK follow-up leaves a 7f gap on block (can frame trap 4f normals in Burnout); 2f extra recovery on Perfect Parry only; if the 1st hit is Perfect Parried, 2nd hit will interrupt any punish slower than 5f startup (trades with 6f attacks); cannot perform follow-up attacks if both hits whiff; carries Counter-hit/Punish Counter advantage through both hits; can juggle after DR~4HP (easier execution but less damaging than his MP Tiger Shot juggle sequence); opponents can beat all follow-ups with invincible reversals (but standard 6f reversals will not punish 214HK)

moves.name: Tiger Nexus
moves.notes: Similar to HK version but faster (can cancel from more starters like 2HP, 4HP launch, and 5HK 2nd hit); combos naturally into all follow-ups including 6HK; cancel into 6HK follow-up leaves a 7f gap on block (can frame trap 4f normals in Burnout); 2f extra recovery on Perfect Parry only; if the 1st hit is Perfect Parried, 2nd hit will interrupt any punish slower than 5f startup (trades with 6f attacks); cannot perform follow-up attacks if both hits whiff; carries Counter-hit/Punish Counter advantage through both hits; opponents can beat all follow-ups with invincible reversals (but standard 6f reversals will not punish 214KK)

moves.name: Nova Tiger
moves.notes: Connects on both standing/crouching opponents; launches opponent into a limited juggle state; combos naturally from 214KK; after blocked 214KK, interruptible 7f blockstring gap (frame trap vs. Burnout); unsafe to reversal Drive Impact and susceptible to Perfect Parry on reaction (becomes DI-safe from 214KK if opponent delays it by 2f or longer); opponent is left inside throw range on block (but Sagat cannot shimmy an immediate throw tech)

moves.name: Mighty Tiger
moves.notes: Mixup tool that is unsafe on block; the threat of overhead makes ~6MK follow-up stronger while the threat of a frame trap makes ~6HK follow-up stronger; safe vs. Burnout but no longer frame traps, making it a weak option; puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state (e.g. after DI wallsplat juggle); causes immediate knockdown on Counter-hit/Punish Counter; safe to reversal Drive Impact after blocked 214KK unless the 6LK input is delayed

moves.name: Greedy Tiger
moves.notes: Whiffs on crouching opponents; 2f extra recovery on whiff; puts opponent into a limited juggle state (only allows 623LP/PP juggle in the corner); frame data vs. crouch from 214KK: -17 oH / -24 oB / -13 onPC; safe to reversal Drive Impact after blocked 214KK; 3f blockstring gap after 214KK (frame trap vs. standing normals but still loses to reversal crouching normals); risky to attempt on block, but the threat of the overhead and frame trap from ~6LK follow-up can condition opponents to stand block or parry; opponent cannot walk back out of throw range on block

moves.name: Nova Tiger
moves.notes: Connects on both standing/crouching opponents; launches opponent into a limited juggle state; only combos naturally from 214HK (requires juggle state for LK/MK versions, like a CH/PC Tiger Nexus); after blocked 214LK/MK, interruptible 9f blockstring gap (5f gap vs. Burnout, loses to 4f normals); after blocked 214HK, interruptible 7f blockstring gap (frame trap vs. Burnout); unsafe to reversal Drive Impact and susceptible to Perfect Parry on reaction (becomes DI-safe from 214HK if opponent delays it by 2f or longer); opponent is left inside throw range on block (but Sagat cannot shimmy an immediate throw tech)

moves.name: Mighty Tiger
moves.notes: Mixup tool that is unsafe on block; the threat of overhead makes ~6MK follow-up stronger while the threat of a frame trap makes ~6HK follow-up stronger; safe vs. Burnout but no longer frame traps (unless the 6LK input is delayed from 214LK/MK); puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state (e.g. after Counter-hit 214LK/MK); causes immediate knockdown on Counter-hit/Punish Counter; loses to reversal Drive Impact after blocked 214LK/MK (but safe after 214HK unless the 6LK input is delayed); if used from a 2-light chain, opponent is in range for Throw or 2LK~5LP chain (too far if starting with 3-light chain)

moves.name: Greedy Tiger
moves.notes: Whiffs on crouching opponents; 2f extra recovery on whiff; puts opponent into a limited juggle state (only allows 623LP/PP juggle in the corner, or 623MP from CH/PC 214LK/MK launch); frame data vs. crouch from 214LK/214MK: -19 oH / -26 oB / KD +51 onPC launch; frame data vs. crouch from 214HK: -17 oH / -24 oB / -13 onPC (214HK keeps opponent crouching on Punish Counter); safe to reversal Drive Impact after blocked 214K; 5f blockstring gap after 214LK/MK (loses to reversal standing/crouching 4f normals); 3f blockstring gap after 214HK (frame trap vs. standing normals but still loses to reversal crouching normals); risky to attempt on block, but the threat of the overhead and frame trap from ~6LK follow-up can condition opponents to stand block or parry; opponent cannot walk back out of throw range on block

moves.name: Tiger Nexus
moves.notes: The only strength of 214K that can combo naturally from 5LP (3-light confirm can reach if point blank, but results in weaker mixup from ~6LK ender); does not frame trap when canceled on block (except from Light normals with Drive Rush or Burnout); combos into 6LK/6MK follow-ups; canceling into the 6HK follow-up leaves a 2f gap on hit / 9f gap on block (loses to 4f normals even in Burnout); Counter-hit/Punish Counter puts the opponent into a limited juggle state that allows the 6HK follow-up to combo; cannot perform follow-up attacks on whiff; opponents can beat all follow-ups with invincible reversals (but standard 6f reversals will not punish 214LK); if the opponent attempts to punish 214LK, the 6LK follow-up will frame trap on block (must delay 6LK vs. Burnout)

moves.name: Tiger Nexus
moves.notes: Combos into 6LK/6MK follow-ups; canceling into the 6HK follow-up leaves a 2f gap on hit / 9f gap on block (loses to 4f normals even in Burnout); Counter-hit/Punish Counter puts the opponent into a limited juggle state that allows the 6HK follow-up to combo; 214MK combos from canceled 2MP/2HP/5HK (these cancels also frame trap on block, with 2HP/5HK > 214MK being DI-safe); cannot perform follow-up attacks on whiff; lacks natural juggle potential but can juggle after DR~4HP (free juggle state) for a powerful 1-bar corner combo (DR~4HP > 214MK, 4HP > 236HK, 623MP); opponents can beat all follow-ups with invincible reversals (but standard 6f reversals will not punish 214MK); if the opponent attempts to punish 214MK, the 6LK follow-up will frame trap on block (must delay 6LK vs. Burnout)

moves.name: Tiger Vanquisher
moves.notes: Cinematic time regenerates ~1.9 Drive bars for Sagat; only 2f startup when canceled from Tiger Uppercut; can be used as a projectile counter from about half screen; slow startup makes it a risky wakeup reversal option; total damage scaling from anti-air Tiger Uppercut is 20-40% depending on which strength was used (weaker strength gives higher scaling)

moves.name: Tiger Vanquisher (CA)
moves.notes: Available at 25% HP or below; cinematic time regenerates ~1.9 Drive bars for Sagat; only 2f startup when canceled from Tiger Uppercut; can be used as a projectile counter from about half screen; slow startup makes it a risky wakeup reversal option; total damage scaling from anti-air Tiger Uppercut is 20-40% depending on which strength was used (weaker strength gives higher scaling)

moves.name: Tiger Cannon
moves.notes: 8-hit Super projectile; can be used while OD Tiger Shot is on-screen (but not meterless Tiger Shot); fast travel speed allows it to be used in long range juggles; projectile speed is not affected by button strength

moves.name: Tiger Knee Crush
moves.notes: Furthest horizontal distance; much better block advantage when spaced at max range; 2nd hit active frames 1-9 whiff on crouching opponents; this means that if the Knee is spaced out so the first hit whiffs, it connects on the 2nd to last active frame vs. crouching opponents (+4 on block); if the 1st hit is crouch blocked, opponent cannot switch to stand block the 2nd hit; puts opponent into a limited juggle state (in the corner, can juggle 623LP if the last 6 active frames connect, or 623MP / SA2 if the final active frame connects); blocked Knee causes a screen shake when Sagat has frame advantage; Sweet Spot occurs when juggling into the 3rd or 4th active frame, dealing 1300 damage (single hit) with a higher spinning juggle launch (ensures a follow-up juggle is possible even midscreen); the 2nd hit's extended Knee hitbox is too high to connect on standing characters on active frames 2-7 (tall characters: active frames 4-6); sets up corner safe jump in certain juggle scenarios (e.g. after juggled 2MP~HP)

moves.name: High Tiger Shot
moves.notes: Fast 1-hit projectile; whiffs on crouching opponents unless they extend an upward hurtbox; puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state; has much better recovery and frame advantage than the Low version; can be used meaty on the opponent's wakeup even if they crouch block, but the opponent can input a crouching button to avoid blocking the projectile; extends a slight projectile invincible arm hurtbox on frames 14-28 and a leg hurtbox on frames 14-42

moves.name: Tiger Knee Crush
moves.notes: 1st hit transitions to a different follow-up on hit, resulting in higher damage and a tumbling +66 knockdown (allows a 623LP juggle in the corner); if 1st hit whiffs, the next 2 hits deal 500 damage each and give a worse knockdown (only 1 hit at farthest ranges); safe on block but usually lands inside the opponent's throw range; 2nd hit active frames 2-10 whiff on crouching opponents; this means that if the Knee is spaced out, it connects on the last active frame vs. crouching opponents (+1 on block); unlike HK Knee, the opponent can switch to stand block after the first hit connects, leaving Sagat at -2; blocked Knee causes a screen shake when Sagat has frame advantage; later hits put opponent into a limited juggle state (in the corner, can juggle 623LP)

moves.name: Tiger Knee Crush
moves.notes: Shortest horizontal distance; no front leg hurtbox on frames 10-12 (helps avoid low pokes); 3f extra landing recovery when absorbed by armor; much better block advantage (up to +2) when spaced at max range; active frames 2-10 whiff on crouching opponents; this means that if the Knee is spaced out so the first active frame whiffs, it always connects on the last active frame vs. crouching opponents (+2 on block, 623LP juggle on hit); puts opponent into a limited juggle state (in the corner, can juggle 623LP if the last active frame connects); blocked Knee causes a screen shake when Sagat has frame advantage; can be whiffed in some situations for a side switch vs. knocked down opponents

moves.name: Low Tiger Shot
moves.notes: Fast 1-hit projectile (speed is not variable); can hit crouching opponents unlike MP/HP High Tiger Shot; has extremely long recovery compared to most projectiles (more vulnerable to jumps, Drive Impact, projectile invuln moves, and Perfect Parry + Drive Rush); the projectile travels low to the ground, preventing many low profile attacks from avoiding it (e.g. Kimberly's slide, A.K.I.'s Sinister Slide); Sagat is in a crouching state for the entire move duration with crouch-sized hurtboxes; puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state; extends a slight projectile invincible arm hurtbox on frames 16-43 and a leg hurtbox on frames 14-50; topmost hurtboxes are vulnerable only to air attacks on frames 1-50 (more vulnerable to jump-ins despite crouching) and are projectile invincible on frames 1-31 to avoid High Tiger Shot (frames 32-50 are still vulnerable)

moves.name: Low Tiger Shot
moves.notes: Fast 2-hit OD projectile; can hit crouching opponents; can be used while a meterless Tiger Shot is still on-screen; the projectile travels low to the ground, preventing many low profile attacks from avoiding it (e.g. Kimberly's slide, A.K.I.'s Sinister Slide); Sagat is in a crouching state for the entire move duration with crouch-sized hurtboxes; puts opponents into a limited juggle state; extends a slight projectile invincible arm hurtbox on frames 16-37 and a leg hurtbox on frames 12-44; topmost hurtboxes are vulnerable only to air attacks on frames 1-44 (more vulnerable to jump-ins despite crouching) and are projectile invincible on frames 1-29 to avoid High Tiger Shot (frames 30-44 are still vulnerable); starter scaling does not apply if only the 2nd hit connects (e.g. clashing with 1-hit OD fireball or breaking Drive Impact armor)

moves.name: Tiger Knee Crush
moves.notes: Medium horizontal distance; no front leg hurtbox on frames 14-15 (helps avoid low pokes); 3f extra landing recovery when absorbed by armor; much better block advantage (up to +3) when spaced at max range; active frames 2-9 whiff on crouching opponents; this means that if the Knee is spaced out so the first active frame whiffs, it connects on the 2nd to last active frame vs. crouching opponents (+2 on block, 623LP juggle on hit); puts opponent into a limited juggle state (in the corner, can juggle 623LP if the last 4 active frames connect); blocked Knee causes a screen shake when Sagat has frame advantage; can be whiffed in some situations for a side switch vs. knocked down opponents; sets up midscreen safe jump in certain juggle scenarios (e.g. after juggled 2MP~HP)

moves.name: High Tiger Shot
moves.notes: Medium speed 1-hit projectile (comparable to a shoto HP fireball, but much slower than Sagat's other projectiles); whiffs on crouching opponents unless they extend an upward hurtbox; puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state (useful juggle tool after 4HP launch); has much better recovery and frame advantage than the Low version; can be used meaty on the opponent's wakeup even if they crouch block, but the opponent can input a crouching button to avoid blocking the projectile; extends a slight projectile invincible arm hurtbox on frames 18-32 and a leg hurtbox on frames 18-42

moves.name: High Tiger Shot
moves.notes: Extremely fast 3-hit OD projectile; slow startup but very powerful in fireball wars once released; can hit crouching opponents unlike the MP/HP High Tiger Shots; can be used while a meterless Tiger Shot is still on-screen; excellent frame advantage on hit or block; puts opponents into a limited juggle state; can juggle into SA1 from anywhere on the screen, and into another OD High Tiger Shot from fullscreen (or at close range vs. cornered opponents); extends a slight projectile invincible arm hurtbox on frames 25-41 and a leg hurtbox on frames 25-48; starter scaling does not apply if only the 3rd hit connects (e.g. clashing with 2-hit OD fireball or breaking Drive Impact armor)

moves.name: Tiger Kick
moves.notes: Has some juggle potential; great range and hitbox priority; can be punished on block by most other sweeps in the game

moves.name: Crouching Heavy Punch
moves.notes: Very long range for a cancelable and hitconfirmable poke; significantly more range on active frames 3-4; topmost hurtbox is vulnerable only to aerial strikes on frames 1-14 (preventing its use as an anti-air), and is projectile invincible on frames 1-19 to avoid High Tiger Shot (frames 20-35 are still vulnerable)

moves.name: Crouching Light Kick
moves.notes: Chains into 5LP/2LP/2LK; low starter that can combo into any 3-light chain from close range

moves.name: Crouching Light Punch
moves.notes: Chains into 5LP/2LP/2LK; excellent range for a 4f jab; high pushback makes tick throw and counter-hit pressure weaker, but also allows Sagat to space himself outside the opponent's reversal normals on block; DR cancel is delayed until after 2nd~3rd recovery frame; topmost hurtbox on frames 1-5 is vulnerable only to aerial strikes (preventing its use as an anti-air)

moves.name: Crouching Medium Kick
moves.notes: Amazing hitbox priority as a neutral poke; can link to 5LP at closer ranges, or into 2MP/5LK on Counter-hit; useful combo/pressure starter out of Drive Rush (but has poor link options near its max range)

moves.name: Crouching Medium Punch
moves.notes: Solid mid-range cancelable poke and buffer tool; 1f extra recovery on block; 3f extra recovery on whiff; significantly more range on active frames 2-3 (more effective linking from +8 or punishing -8 moves); cancelable into 2 different Target Combo follow-ups with different hitconfirm timings (requires Punish Counter or Drive Rush for 2MP~HP combo); topmost hurtbox is vulnerable only to aerial strikes on frames 1-9 (preventing its use as an anti-air), and is projectile invincible on frames 1-14 to avoid High Tiger Shot (frames 15-26 are still vulnerable)

moves.name: Tiger Rise
moves.notes: 3f blockstring gap between hits; harder to confirm into from 2MP but combos naturally; launch only allows a canceled Super but no other follow-up juggles; easily hitconfirmed into Super even if only the 2nd hit connects as a frame trap; higher KD advantage when juggled into

moves.name: Tiger Slash
moves.notes: Combos after Punish Counter or Drive Rush 2MP only; causes limited juggle OTG bounce vs. airborne opponents

moves.name: Tiger Monolith
moves.notes: Tall hitbox on 2nd hit, but also extends a tall hurtbox with no anti-air invincibility (likely to lose/trade with jump-ins); cannot hit cross-up; 2nd hit whiffs on crouch blocking opponents (3f worse on block and not cancelable); cancel does not occur until the 2nd hit's active frames (still executes on hit even if the 2nd hit whiffs); puts opponents into a limited juggle state (can combo into 236MP, DR~delay 4HP > 236HK, 623MP for great midscreen damage and corner carry); free juggle state from DR~4HP, allowing a more optimal corner juggle: > 214MK, 4HP > 236HK, 623MP; launches higher on Counter-hit/Punish Counter (KD +41) or on airborne opponents (KD +40); 1st hit puts opponent into a free juggle OTG bounce state that is usually overwritten by the 2nd hit (but can still occur on trades or when hitting extended hurtboxes)

moves.name: Tiger Carry
moves.notes: Side switch; no true oki after throwing opponent into the corner, but can pressure with Tiger Shot, MK/HK Knee, or spaced Drive Rush normals; a successful Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender; Throw Escape is awarded to a random player if input simultaneously

moves.name: Back Taunt
moves.notes: "If you're on a path to attain strength, show me your worth!"

moves.name: Standing Heavy Kick
moves.notes: Upper Body/Leg hurtbox is anti-air invincible on frames 9-15 (solid anti-air against midrange jumps); cannot hit cross-up; 1st hit forces stand on hit; 2nd hit whiffs on crouching opponents (2f worse on block); 4f extra recovery if both hits whiff; 1st hit deals extra hitstun, allowing a natural combo into 214HK; deals full damage / Drive damage / Meter gain even if only the 2nd hit connects; 1st hit puts airborne opponents into a free juggle state (limited juggle if comboed from a wallsplat or airborne crumple), then air resets on the 2nd hit; 2nd hit only has juggle potential after the 1st hit connects; the first 11 recovery frames extend a wide leg hurtbox making it more easily whiff punished by standing normals; carries counter-hit/Punish Counter advantage through both hits

moves.name: Standing Heavy Punch
moves.notes: 3f extra recovery on whiff; huge range poke with a hitconfirmable TC follow-up; the first 10 recovery frames extend a wide arm-height hurtbox making it easily whiff punished by standing normals

moves.name: Tiger Sting
moves.notes: Both hits are always a true blockstring; hitconfirmable knockdown from a very strong midrange poke; sets up a KD +42 safe jump when juggled into (like after a DI wallsplat on hit/block)

moves.name: Standing Light Kick
moves.notes: Long range but slow startup (more comparable to a medium normal); 2f extra recovery on whiff; great whiff punish tool that combos consistently into 623HP on Punish Counter; input overlap with 6LK Step Low Kick makes it harder to walk forward and poke in neutral; DR cancel is delayed until after 2nd recovery frame

moves.name: Standing Light Punch
moves.notes: Chains into 5LP/2LP/2LK; great range for a chainable 5f jab (but slightly shorter than a standard shoto 5LK); DR cancel is delayed until after 2nd recovery frame; Sagat's only light normal that combos naturally into 214LK

moves.name: Standing Medium Kick
moves.notes: Very long poke with a semi-hitconfirmable TC follow-up; more range vs. standing opponents (the tip of the hitbox whiffs on crouching opponents); the first 10 recovery frames extend a wide leg hurtbox making it more easily whiff punished by standing normals

moves.name: Step Middle Kick
moves.notes: 3f blockstring gap between hits; somewhat hitconfirmable knockdown from a very strong midrange poke; puts opponent into a limited juggle state (can combo 623LP after DI wallsplat on hit)

moves.name: Standing Medium Punch
moves.notes: Core pressure tool for frame traps (5MPx2 sets up a trade combo vs. most reversal 4f normals); pushback on block is too far for a throw mixup without Drive Rush; links consistently into 2MP on counter-hit or into 5HK on Punish Counter (very strong Drive Reversal punish option); on regular hit can lead to 5MP, 5MP, 5LP combo

moves.name: Neutral Taunt
moves.notes: "If you desire the throne, stand tall against the emperor."

moves.name: Tiger Uppercut
moves.notes: Extremely long range but slow startup (cannot combo naturally from light normals, but works well as a combo ender from 5LK whiff punish); deals 600 less damage on active frames 3-10; cannot hit cross-up; can be charged into a much stronger version by holding the button 24 frames; releasing the button early results in uncharged 623HP with 8f startup after release; if partially charged, the Air Invuln is 1-9f then 1-11f after the button is released, and the airborne frames are 12-57f after the button is released; puts opponent into a limited juggle state (allows SA3 cancel on active frames 1-2 only)

moves.name: Tiger Uppercut (hold)
moves.notes: Button must be held 24f for fully charged version; causes a wall splat on hit that leaves Sagat at a fixed distance (no follow-up combo); deals 1100 less damage on active frames 4-10 with no wallsplat animation (KD +29 on active frame 4); cannot hit cross-up; 1st hit puts opponent into a limited juggle state (allows SA3 cancel on active frames 1-3 only)

moves.name: Tiger Uppercut
moves.notes: Sagat's primary anti-air with fast startup but short range; deals 300 less damage on active frames 4-10; cannot hit cross-up; puts opponent into a limited juggle state (allows SA3 cancel on active frames 1-2 only)

moves.name: Tiger Uppercut
moves.notes: Much more range than LP version for mid-range anti airs and more consistent cancels from light normals; much slower startup (limits usefulness in many juggles); forward movement makes Sagat more likely to whiff under an opponent's jump-in; deals 600 less damage on active frames 4-10; cannot hit cross-up; puts opponent into a limited juggle state (allows SA3 cancel on active frames 1-2 only)

moves.name: Tiger Uppercut
moves.notes: Sagat's main reversal; slightly slower than most OD reversals (can be safejabbed by Dee Jay 5LP but is otherwise reliable); deals less damage if it connects on later active frames (1st hit deals significant portion of overall damage); cannot hit cross-up

moves.name: Step High Kick
moves.notes: Upper Body/Leg hurtbox is anti-air invincible on frames 14-19 (useful as a predictive long range anti-air); whiffs on crouching opponents; puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state; Punish Counter staggers grounded opponents and puts airborne opponents into a free juggle state; 3f fewer total frames on block/parry/armor (active frames end upon contact, with variable recovery depending on which active frame connected); the first 5 recovery frames extend a wide hurtbox where the kicking leg was (too high for many attacks to easily connect as a whiff punish); extends hurtbox 1f before active that is vulnerable to projectiles; useful in Drive Rush cancel routes from 2HP/5HK/2MP~HP (but the pushback prevents Sagat's usual midscreen link of 4HP > 236MP, juggle DR~4HP)

moves.name: Tiger Twin Babel (Block)
moves.notes: Performed by inputting 6HPHK during blockstun; 5f extra recovery on hit; freezes the screen for 4f during startup; see Drive Reversal.

moves.name: Tiger Twin Babel (Recovery)
moves.notes: Performed by holding 6HPHK on wakeup; 5f extra recovery on hit; does not have any screen freeze except for a 12f freeze when interacting with the opponent's throw hitbox (this also refunds 1 Drive bar after punishing the throw); see Drive Reversal.

moves.name: Step Low Kick
moves.notes: Long range advancing low poke that leaves Sagat close for a strike/throw mixup on hit while remaining safe on block; 3f extra recovery on whiff; can link into light normals on Counter-hit, or into 2MP after Drive Rush or Punish Counter; knocks down airborne opponents (KD +35~38) when juggled into (but has no juggle potential on its own); the first 7 recovery frames extend a wide foot hurtbox making it more easily whiff punished by low-reaching normals

moves.name: Tiger Heavy Elbow
moves.notes: Spike knockdown vs. airborne opponents; Drive Rush gives a combo into 2MP (no real strike/throw pressure on block); meaty timing allows a follow-up link (up to +5/0 on final active frame)

moves.name: Forward Taunt
moves.notes: "The emperor's strength is peerless. However, it would be my pleasure to test your strength!"

moves.name: Tiger Punishment
moves.notes: See Drive Impact. Airborne connect gives spinning juggle state on Punish Counter or corner Wall Splat with variable height.

moves.name: Jumping Heavy Kick
moves.notes: Longest horizontal range; puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state; lower body projectile invuln 10-21f (if used immediately on the way up, can avoid the 2nd hit of JP's OD Amnesia bombs)

moves.name: Jumping Heavy Punch
moves.notes: Strong downward attack angle; spike knockdown vs. airborne opponents; lower body projectile invuln 10-22f (cannot be used to avoid the 2nd hit of JP's OD Amnesia bombs)

moves.name: Jumping Light Kick
moves.notes: Cross-up; can be used as a fuzzy instant overhead

moves.name: Jumping Light Punch
moves.notes: Fast air-to-air with solid horizontal range

moves.name: Jumping Medium Kick
moves.notes: Long horizontal range (barely shorter than j.HK) with a better downward attack angle and nearly identical hitstun and blockstun; lower body projectile invuln 8-25f except around attack hitbox (cannot be used to avoid the 2nd hit of JP's OD Amnesia bombs)

moves.name: Jumping Medium Punch
moves.notes: 2 hits; puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state; if 1st hit is stand blocked, the 2nd hit will not hit overhead against crouch block; lower body projectile invuln 8-22f (if used immediately on the way up, can avoid the 2nd hit of JP's OD Amnesia bombs)

moves.name: Tiger Hang
moves.notes: Can use Drive Rush for a corner throw loop with 4f timing on standard characters; a successful Throw Escape builds 0.5 Drive bars for the defender; Throw Escape is awarded to a random player if input simultaneously

moves.name: Drive Parry
moves.notes: See Drive Parry. Perfect Parrying has only 1F of recovery and disables the opponent from canceling their attack. Perfect Parrying projectiles puts you into fixed 11 frames of recovery. After a Perfect Parry, all Super Gauge gain is reduced by 20% and Drive Gauge gain/damage is reduced by 50% for the entire punish combo.

moves.name: Drive Rush Cancel
moves.notes: See Drive Rush; 3-bar version performed on hit/block from a cancelable normal; can also be performed on whiff from cancelable light normals; startup refers to minimum time before an attack can cancel the Drive Rush animation; the first 15 recovery frames are cancelable into any attack; the final 22 recovery frames are cancelable into any attack or movement option or blocking (except Parry); only Normal and Command Normal attacks are enhanced with +4 frame advantage and improved juggle properties

moves.name: Parry Drive Rush
moves.notes: See Drive Rush; 1-bar version performed out of a Parry; startup refers to minimum time before an attack can cancel the Drive Rush animation (if performed immediately after a successful Parry, only 1+8 startup); the first 15 recovery frames are cancelable into any attack; the final 22 recovery frames are cancelable into any attack or movement option or blocking (except Parry); only Normal and Command Normal attacks are enhanced with +4 frame advantage and improved juggle properties; Distance: 0.546 (min/throw), 1.869 (min/block), 3.156 (max/final DR frame)

patches.summary: Ingrid Release. Minor system changes and bug fixes.
notes: OD Low Tiger Shot (236LPMP or 236LPHP)
Fixed issue where inputting 236LPMP while holding down the HP button would result in a MP High Tiger Shot

patches.summary: Alex Release. Balance changes for all characters.
notes: 5LK reduced pushback on hit for combo consistency
2MP whiff recovery increased 17 → 19
Tiger Heavy Elbow (6MP) blockstun 20 → 19; Block Advantage -2 → -3; increased pushback on block

patches.summary: Bug fixes and minor adjustments, primarily for Elena, Mai, and Sagat.
notes: 2LK pushback reduced on hit/block for more consistent hitconfirms
2MK Hit Advantage +4 → +5; hitstun 25 → 26
Gives a natural link to 5LP, a CH link to 5LK/2MP, and a DR/PC link to itself at farther ranges
Tiger Monolith (4HP) 1st hit active frames increased 2 → 3 (more consistent juggle tool, does not affect anti-air frames)
Charged HP Tiger Uppercut (623[HP]) now gives the stronger cinematic hit up to the 3rd active frame instead of only frames 1-2; collision box expanded upward on active frames 1-2
This slightly increases the max range of the strong hit and makes it more consistent in some high juggles
HK Tiger Knee (236HK) expanded combo-only hitbox of 2nd hit upward to prevent it from whiffing when 1st hit connects (does not apply to "sweet spot" connect)
LK/MK Tiger Nexus (214LK/214MK) increased pushback on hit; increased forward movement during startup; increased horizontal blowback on airborne hit
More consistent in grounded confirms (e.g. 3 lights > 214LK), while keeping juggle scenarios intact
Mighty Tiger (214K/KK~6LK) increased pushback on hit; increased horizontal blowback on airborne hit
If 214LK~6LK is used from a 2-light confirm, opponent is in range for Throw or 2LK~5LP mixup; does not work from new 3-light confirm
Greedy Tiger (214K/KK~6MK) Drive Damage increased 6000 → 8000
Nova Tiger (214K/KK~6HK) reduced pushback on block
Can now throw opponents who back walk, but can no longer shimmy unless opponent delays throw tech at least 3f
